Qualitative observation; mechanism remains a hypothesis Evidence → Learning → Change Evidence VUAA1 produced a faint green-fluorescence increase, too weak to quantify. The observation prompted review of reporter abundance and localization. Learning Initial hypothesis (poor Orco expression) was challenged by construct-map re-examination: GCaMP6 is IRES-downstream , so reduced reporter abundance is a plausible explanation for the weak signal — a mechanistic hypothesis, not a measured diagnosis. Change Redesign the reporting module as a translational fusion (Cycle 3) to restore 1:1 stoichiometry and pore-proximal sensing. Intended signal path 1 Orco receptor / channel → 2 Ca²⁺ influx / microdomain → 3 GCaMP sensor → 4 Fluorescence optical report VUAA1 challenges the combined Orco–calcium–reporter pathway. Observation Real but weak fluorescence response to VUAA1 ↓ Initial hypothesis Poor Orco expression ↓ Re-examination GCaMP6 sits downstream of the IRES ; Orco is the upstream, cap-dependent cistron ↓ Revised hypothesis Reporter abundance and/or distance from the Ca²⁺ microdomain may be limiting signal amplitude Design The bicistronic cassette placed Orco upstream of an IRES and GCaMP downstream: CMV → Orco → STOP → IRES → GCaMP → STOP . Separate proteins preserved the bicistronic arrangement used in the visibly fluorescent OR–IRES–mCherry modules. We tested whether downstream GCaMP provided enough signal for a transient calcium response. Build We synthesized Orco–IRES–GCaMP and transfected HEK293. Orco and cytosolic GCaMP remained separate proteins, with GCaMP translated downstream of the IRES. Test Test evidence: Preliminary reporter observation; quantitative comparison not archived. We challenged the pathway with VUAA1, an Orco agonist [2] . The green-fluorescence increase was visible on close inspection but too weak for reliable quantification. This observation did not resolve receptor abundance, localization, reporter abundance, calcium handling or imaging limitations. Learn The map placed Orco in the cap-dependent upstream position and GCaMP downstream of the IRES, suggesting a reporter-expression bottleneck [3] . GCaMP fluorescence also depends on calcium state [4] ; a dim resting image cannot by itself establish failed expression. Reporter proximity to the channel was a second hypothesis. Neither abundance nor localization was measured independently. Redesign We chose a single-ORF GCaMP6f–linker–Orco fusion to address translation stoichiometry and channel proximity together. A 2A design would still produce separate proteins. Because several features changed together, any fusion comparison concerns the whole redesign. Key decision Selected a single-ORF, pore-proximal reporter architecture. Acceptance criteria vs observed result Success criterion (defined in advance) VUAA1-evoked ΔF/F₀ large enough to quantify on the plate reader, clearly separated from vehicle Response abolished in Ca²⁺-free buffer (extracellular Ca²⁺ influx, not sensor artefact) Observed result ○ No comparison supplied — no direct IRES-versus-fusion functional comparison. Design We placed GCaMP6f at the Orco N terminus through a flexible (GGGGS)₃ linker to coordinate translation and place the reporter near the channel. Cytosolic N-terminal placement follows insect OR/Orco topology [5] [6] . Fusion effects on folding, localization and channel function remain unresolved. Build The historical pre-synthesis review checked reading frame, internal stops, Kozak context, domain order, orientation and cloning junctions. That version recorded 2,856 bp / 951 amino acids with no internal stop and Kozak sequence GCCACCATGG . Synonymous codons diversified the three repeated 15-bp linker units while retaining the peptide sequence. The final 8,293-bp pcDNA3.1(+) plasmid was synthesised, the vendor sequence matched the intended construct, and the part was recorded as BBa_26E11Z80 . Test Test evidence: Construct review and fixed-field microscopy. The available microscopy record now covers 25 fields across 12 conditions before G418 selection. The analysis on Results quantifies reporter-positive fractions among eligible segmented DAPI objects; dense regions limit the denominator, and the fields are not independent biological replicates. These fixed images document fluorescence detectability, not a live calcium-response comparison. Learn Sequence correctness, detectable fluorescence and dynamic sensor function are separate outcomes. Dim resting GCaMP6f and crowded nuclei limit simple cell-fraction estimates. Redesign The diagnostic scheme separates reporter competence with ionomycin from Orco-linked response with VUAA1. Electrical design audit and professional review Evidence → Learning → Change Evidence August 2 V1 PCB archive Team archive : 73 DRC violations ; 4 unconnected items ; 7 ERC errors ; 11 ERC warnings ( Figure E-H1B ). Followed by iST Group schematic/layout review. Manufacturing of V1 was stopped. Learning High gain is not the same as high sensitivity. At 100 MΩ, contamination, humidity, flux residue, incorrect guarding, or nearby switching can rival the photodiode current. A high-resolution ADC cannot recover information corrupted before digitization. Change Objective shifted from “amplify fluorescence as much as possible” to preserve measurement integrity across the analog/optical chain — driving the concrete V2 redesign listed under Redesign. Conceptual pivot Before “Amplify the fluorescence as much as possible” ↓ After “Preserve measurement integrity throughout the entire analog and optical chain.” Hardware V1 → V2 (measurement integrity) Before · V1 After · V2 redesign Showing Before · V1 Gain-first V1 100 MΩ TIA emphasis for maximum amplification Longer high-impedance PD/TIA routing risk Shared analog/digital supply priorities Stopped before fab after DRC/ERC + review Integrity-first V2 Shorter PD–LMP7721 path + guarded region ADS8866 symbol rebuilt; 3-wire CS + damping Separate 3V3_ANA / 3V3_DIG rails Improved decoupling and return-current management Design V1 combined LED excitation, a sample, photodiode, LMP7721 TIA, ADS8866 ADC and ESP32. The four-layer board included 100 MΩ feedback, four LED channels, power regulation and a Raspberry Pi interface. The review examined whether layout, supplies and the ADC interface preserved the signal at this gain. Build V1 included a schematic, PCB layout, BOM, footprints, 3D models and DRC/ERC reports. The board was not fabricated. The team prepared the design; iST Group reviewed the high-impedance detector region and mixed-signal interfaces. Test Test evidence: Archived computational DRC / ERC audit. The V1 archive recorded 73 DRC violations, four unconnected items, seven ERC errors and 11 ERC warnings , covering clearance, solder mask, incomplete nets, guards, power rules and symbol/footprint consistency. V1 was not fabrication-ready. Professional review covered LMP7721 pins and guarding, photodiode pads, TIA placement, ADS8866/reference decoupling, SAR input behavior, ESP32 EN/BOOT and critical capacitors. Learn At 100 MΩ, leakage from long traces, poor guarding, humidity or flux residue can rival photocurrent. More ADC resolution cannot recover a corrupted analog signal. The ADC symbol also required correction against its datasheet. The design objective shifted from gain alone to control of optical and electrical interference. Redesign V2 shortens the photodiode–LMP7721 high-impedance path and adds guarding around the detector/TIA feedback region. The ADC symbol was rebuilt from the ADS8866 pinout; the design uses the intended three-wire CS arrangement with DIN high and damping on SCLK/CONVST. Analog and digital 3.3 V supplies, decoupling and return-current paths were separated or reorganized. Cycle 2 then reviewed the need for a second processor. Key decision Stop V1 before fab; treat DRC/ERC plus professional review as the cycle’s Test evidence; redesign V2 around measurement integrity rather than maximum gain. Optical and gas computations completed Design The enclosure brief required a compact footprint, real connector access, a fan below the PCB, black-sleeved flat wells, fewer printed parts and a clear assembly sequence. The resulting nominal envelope is 108 × 108 × 66 mm, with LED-based well positions and a removable seal-loading plate. We modeled collection geometry, cross-well transfer and gas redirection within the shared enclosure. Build The package contains editable CAD and individual STLs for eight operating prints, including an integrated fan cradle and gas deflector. The optical model represents clear flat-bottom wells, the off-center detector proxy, filter/seal and opaque carrier. The gas model represents the common plenum and alternative perforated or directional features. Before the current enclosure, the archive retained a larger integrated body, a removable service tray and a hinged lid. Hardware simulations / Discussion

Discussion

Optical geometry, filtering and transport impose different limits. Nonzero optical mixing calls for a measured channel-mixing matrix; LED-synchronous leakage calls for an illuminated blank. Gas-surface arrival establishes when the chamber supplies a well, while liquid diffusion determines the separate path to bottom-attached cells. A single end-to-end response time cannot be inferred by substituting one for another.

The shelf is a compact way to redirect flow, not the fastest geometry in every comparison. The selected 3 mL/min condition provides timing margin against the stated 60 s criterion; grid sensitivity makes a near-threshold 2.5 mL/min result less decisive. Together with the membrane sweep, these comparisons favor measurable delivery and a simple no-film baseline over adding uncharacterized layers.

The optical and filter results are predictions under their stated source and noise assumptions. The constructed OD4 disc also differs from the selected film in mounting geometry; its modeled performance does not establish compatibility with the reader.

The gas calculation ends above the liquid surface; this separate layer model describes subsequent transport. Its diffusivities and partition coefficients are sensitivity inputs. No-film delivery and recovery at the cell plane provide the physical comparison for any proposed membrane.

Physical checks must cover blank and dye calibration, actual detector/filter response, one fluorescent source well at a time, LED-synchronous background and noise, and assembled-path flow, pressure and interface concentration history. These measurements test the design decisions rather than being supplied by the simulations.

The four strong same-well entries contribute substantially to this association. Comparing only the 12 cross-well entries gives Pearson r = 0.257, so the overall correlation does not establish quantitative agreement of the leakage pattern. The liquid-standard and floor-layer source conditions also differ, and the measured response includes electronic effects.

The SE excludes uncertain LED power, resin optics, detector orientation, filter-angle response and cellular expression.

The predicted photodiode currents describe the optical input; they do not include measured electronics or cell responses.
